previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, GERD, pseudotumor cerebri, and multiple recent hospitalizations for dyspnea was admitted for shortness of breath and chest tightness after cleaning her home. Initial concern for asthma exacerbation was reconsidered due to lack of wheezing, suboptimal response to bronchodilators, and normal chest imaging. Pulmonary function tests showed poor airflow without obstructive pattern, leading to a diagnosis of vocal cord dysfunction. She improved with supportive care and a short steroid taper. Chronic conditions were managed, including insulin for steroid-induced hyperglycemia. She was discharged home with a prednisone taper, continued home medications, and follow-up planned with pulmonary and psychiatry for breathing techniques and vocal cord evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo HTN ___ primary aldosteronism, OSA, HLD, DM-II, obesity, 
migraine, pseudotumor cerebrii, LVH with grade II systolic 
dysfcn presenting with hypertensive urgency and headache.  
.  
# HTN urgency: Patient presented with systolic BP in 170s, but 
normal EKG (except for sinus brady and prolonged QTc), normal 
cardiac enzymes x3. UA does not show proteinuria, and creatinine 
is WNL. She has no papilledema or AV nicking/copper wiring. 
Chest x-ray shows no s/s volume overload or mediastinal 
widening. TSH was found to be within normal limits. Per 
assessment of the primary team and neurology consult, her 
headache was consistent with migraine pain rather than 
hypertension. Pt has a long history of hypertension secondary to 
primary hyperaldosteronism which had been poorly controlled on 
her current med regimen of amlodipine and propranolol. Other 
factors contributing to her HTN are her OSA as well as her 
current headache pain. Her blood pressure was well controlled 
with the addition of captopril 12.5 mg TID during 
hospitalization. Her home doses of amlodipine 10mg daily and 
propranolol 20 mg BID were continued, but propranolol had to be 
held per holding parameters for most of hospitalization due to 
pt's sinus bradycardia. On discharge, she was transitioned to 
enalapril 5mg po daily for more convenient dosing regimen (no 
lisinopril as caused pt ""fatigue"" in the past). Her propranolol 
was continued as potentially helpful in migraine prophylaxis and 
to prevent beta blocker withdrawal, but was reduced to 20mg 
daily as BP had been well controlled despite holding 
propranolol. Her amlodipine 10mg daily was continued. PCP was 
emailed and informed of changes in BP meds.  
.  
# HEADACHE: Pt p/w 1.5 weeks of frontal HA and photophobia, the 
same pain as her migraine headaches but more intense and longer 
duration than usual. Initial differential diagnosis was migraine 
headache vs. pseudotumor cerebrii vs. hypertensive emergency. 
Blood pressure was quickly controlled on captopril and headaches 
persisted, so HTN ruled out as cause of HA. Pseudotumor cerebrii 
also deemed extremely unlikely as pt had normal cranial nerve 
exam (extraocular movements intact, visual fields full), normal 
fundoscopic exam and HA not worsened by positional changes. 
Neurology consulted and agreed with this. As her HAs were same 
as migraines in quality and a/w photophobia, this was deemed to 
be migraine pain. Unfortunately, pt not candidate for triptan or 
ergot therapy as she is on SSRI (celexa) and has risk factors 
for CAD, both of which are contraindications. Cannot take NSAIDs 
as they cause rash. During hospitalization, her headache 
improved with PO oxycodone and PO standing tylenol. Neurology 
consult suggested intranasal stadol (combination opioid receptor 
agonist/antagonist) but this was unfortunately prohibitively 
expensive as pt is on free care plan. She was therefore 
disharged on a short course of oxycodone 2.5mg PO q6 hours and 
tylenol. Also continued on her home acetazolamide (for 
pseudotumor) and topomax. She was also scheduled for an 
outpatient appointment with her former neurologist Dr. 
___, to follow up on her headaches.   
.
# CHEST PAIN. Initial ddx was ischemic demand secondary to 
hypertension vs. anxiety. EKG showed no ischemic changes, and 
cardiac enzymes were flat. Pt has no h/o CAD and has had normal 
persantine stress test and CT coronary angiogram in past. Chest 
pain not a/w activity. Most likely secondary to anxiety. She 
was, however, continued on her ASA and simvastatin, and was sent 
home on lisinopril and propranolol per above problems. 
. 
# Prolonged QTc: Present on EKG from ___ ___s on this 
admission. On further investigation, pt was found to be on three 
potentially QTc prolonging medications: celexa, topomax and 
tizanidine. As celexa and topomax were more helpful and 
important in pt's current management, the tizanidine was 
discontinued on discharge.

during hospitalization.
